sanskrit: yathādityaḥ samudyan vai tamaḥ sarvaṃ vyapohati evaṃ kalyāṇam ātiṣṭhan sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: Just as the sun rising dispels all darkness, so one who abides in virtue is freed from all sins.

sanskrit: pāpānāṃ viddhy adhiṣṭhānaṃ lobham eva dvijottama lubdhāḥ pāpaṃ vyavasyanti narā nātibahuśrutāḥ adharmā dharmarūpeṇa tṛṇaiḥ kūpā ivāvṛtāḥ
english: Know that greed alone is the seat of all sins, O best of twice-born. The greedy and the poorly learned commit sin; those who follow unrighteousness under the guise of righteousness are like wells covered with grass.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ damaḥ pavitrāṇi pralāpā dharmasaṃśritāḥ sarvaṃ hi vidyate teṣu śiṣṭācāraḥ sudurlabhaḥ
english: For them, self-restraint and purifications are mere talk cloaked in dharma; everything may be found in them, yet the conduct of the righteous is exceedingly rare.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca sa tu vipro mahāprājño dharmavyādham apṛcchata śiṣṭācāraṃ katham ahaṃ vidyām iti narottama etan mahāmate vyādha prabravīhi yathātatham
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then that brahmin, most learned, asked the Dharma-Hunter: 'How may I know the conduct of the righteous, O best of men? Tell me truly, O hunter of great wisdom, exactly as it is.'

sanskrit: vyādha uvāca yajño dānaṃ tapo vedāḥ satyaṃ ca dvijasattama pañcaitāni pavitrāṇi śiṣṭācāreṣu nityadā
english: The hunter said: Sacrifice, charity, austerity, the Vedas, and truth, O best of twice-born — these five are always the purifications found in the conduct of the righteous.

sanskrit: kāmakrodhau vaśe kṛtvā dambhaṃ lobham anārjavam dharma ity eva saṃtuṣṭās te śiṣṭāḥ śiṣṭasaṃmatāḥ
english: Those who have subdued desire and anger, who have renounced pretense, greed, and dishonesty, who are satisfied with dharma alone — they are the righteous, honored by the righteous.

sanskrit: na teṣāṃ vidyate 'vṛttaṃ yajñasvādhyāyaśīlinām ācārapālanaṃ caiva dvitīyaṃ śiṣṭalakṣaṇam
english: For those devoted to sacrifice and self-study there is no transgression; and observance of right conduct is indeed the second mark of the righteous.

sanskrit: guruśuśrūṣaṇaṃ satyam akrodho dānam eva ca etac catuṣṭayaṃ brahmañ śiṣṭācāreṣu nityadā
english: Service to the teacher, truthfulness, freedom from anger, and charity — these four, O brahmin, are always present in the conduct of the righteous.

sanskrit: śiṣṭācāre manaḥ kṛtvā pratiṣṭhāpya ca sarvaśaḥ yām ayaṃ labhate tuṣṭiṃ sā na śakyā hy ato 'nyathā
english: Fixing one's mind on righteous conduct and establishing oneself therein in every way, the satisfaction one obtains cannot be had by any other means.

sanskrit: vedasyopaniṣat satyaṃ satyasyopaniṣad damaḥ damasyopaniṣat tyāgaḥ śiṣṭācāreṣu nityadā
english: The secret teaching of the Veda is truth; the secret teaching of truth is self-restraint; the secret teaching of restraint is renunciation — these are always present in the conduct of the righteous.

sanskrit: ye tu dharmam asūyante buddhimohānvitā narāḥ apathā gacchatāṃ teṣām anuyātāpi pīḍyate
english: Those persons deluded in intellect who revile dharma travel the wrong path; even one who follows such people is harmed.

sanskrit: ye tu śiṣṭāḥ suniyatāḥ śrutityāgaparāyaṇāḥ dharmyaṃ panthānam ārūḍhāḥ satyadharmaparāyaṇāḥ
english: But those who are righteous, well-controlled, devoted to the knowledge of scripture and renunciation, who have mounted the path of dharma and are devoted to truth and righteousness —

sanskrit: niyacchanti parāṃ buddhiṃ śiṣṭācārānvitā narāḥ upādhyāyamate yuktāḥ sthityā dharmārthadarśinaḥ
english: — such persons endowed with righteous conduct restrain the highest intellect; established in the teaching of their preceptors, steadfast, they perceive dharma and its true purpose.

sanskrit: nāstikān bhinnamaryādān krūrān pāpamatau sthitān tyaja tāñ jñānam āśritya dhārmikān upasevya ca
english: Abandon atheists, those who transgress boundaries, the cruel, and those fixed in sinful thought; taking refuge in wisdom, associate instead with the righteous.

sanskrit: kāmalobhagrahākīrṇāṃ pañcendriyajalāṃ nadīm nāvaṃ dhṛtimayīṃ kṛtvā janmadurgāṇi saṃtara
english: Making fortitude your boat, cross the river of the five senses crowded with the demons of desire and greed, and traverse the difficult passages of existence.

sanskrit: krameṇa saṃcito dharmo buddhiyogamayo mahān śiṣṭācāre bhavet sādhū rāgaḥ śukleva vāsasi
english: Dharma accumulated gradually through the yoga of wisdom becomes great; attachment to righteous conduct in the virtuous is like whiteness in a garment.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā satyavacanaṃ sarvabhūtahitaṃ param ahiṃsā paramo dharmaḥ sa ca satye pratiṣṭhitaḥ satye kṛtvā pratiṣṭhāṃ tu pravartante pravṛttayaḥ
english: Non-violence, truthful speech, and the highest good of all beings — non-violence is the supreme dharma, and it is established in truth; when one establishes oneself in truth, all one's activities proceed rightly.

sanskrit: satyam eva garīyas tu śiṣṭācāraniṣevitam ācāraś ca satāṃ dharmaḥ santaś cācāralakṣaṇāḥ
english: Truth alone is most weighty when practiced in the conduct of the righteous; the conduct of the good is indeed dharma, and the good are known by their conduct.

sanskrit: yo yathāprakṛtir jantuḥ svāṃ svāṃ prakṛtim aśnute pāpātmā krodhakāmādīn doṣān āpnoty anātmavān
english: Whatever is the nature of a creature, it experiences that very nature; the sinful soul, lacking self-mastery, incurs the faults of anger, desire, and the like.

sanskrit: ārambho nyāyayukto yaḥ sa hi dharma iti smṛtaḥ anācāras tv adharmeti etac chiṣṭānuśāsanam
english: Whatever undertaking is joined with justice is remembered as dharma; misconduct indeed is adharma — this is the teaching of the righteous.

sanskrit: akrudhyanto 'nasūyanto nirahaṃkāramatsarāḥ ṛjavaḥ śamasaṃpannāḥ śiṣṭācārā bhavanti te
english: Those who do not become angry, who do not envy, who are free from ego and jealousy, who are upright and endowed with tranquility — they possess the conduct of the righteous.

sanskrit: traividyavṛddhāḥ śucayo vṛttavanto manasvinaḥ guruśuśrūṣavo dāntāḥ śiṣṭācārā bhavanty uta
english: Those accomplished in the three Vedas, the pure, those of good character, the high-minded, those devoted to serving their teachers, the self-controlled — they too possess righteous conduct.

sanskrit: teṣām adīnasattvānāṃ duṣkarācārakarmaṇām svaiḥ karmabhiḥ satkṛtānāṃ ghoratvaṃ saṃpraṇaśyati
english: Of those of undepressed spirit who practice difficult austerities and are honored by their own deeds, even the harshness of their deeds completely disappears.

sanskrit: taṃ sadācāram āścaryaṃ purāṇaṃ śāśvataṃ dhruvam dharmaṃ dharmeṇa paśyantaḥ svargaṃ yānti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: Seeing that wondrous, ancient, eternal, and immovable good conduct as dharma through dharma, the wise attain heaven.

sanskrit: āstikā mānahīnāś ca dvijātijanapūjakāḥ śrutavṛttopasaṃpannāḥ te santaḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who are believers, free from pride, who honor the twice-born community, who are endowed with learning and good conduct — such righteous ones are bound for heaven.

sanskrit: vedoktaḥ paramo dharmo dharmaśāstreṣu cāparaḥ śiṣṭācīrṇaś ca śiṣṭānāṃ trividhaṃ dharmalakṣaṇam
english: The supreme dharma declared in the Vedas, the other in the law-treatises, and that practiced by the righteous — these are the threefold marks of dharma.

sanskrit: pāraṇaṃ cāpi vidyānāṃ tīrthānām avagāhanam kṣamā satyārjavaṃ śaucaṃ śiṣṭācāranidarśanam
english: Mastery of the sciences, immersion in sacred fords, forbearance, truthfulness, straightforwardness, and purity — these are demonstrations of righteous conduct.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtadayāvanto ahiṃsāniratāḥ sadā paruṣaṃ na prabhāṣante sadā santo dvijapriyāḥ
english: Those who are compassionate toward all beings, always devoted to non-violence, who never speak harshly — such good people are always dear to the twice-born.

sanskrit: śubhānām aśubhānāṃ ca karmaṇāṃ phalasaṃcaye vipākam abhijānanti te śiṣṭāḥ śiṣṭasaṃmatāḥ
english: Those who know the ripening of the accumulated fruits of both auspicious and inauspicious deeds — they are the righteous, honored by the righteous.

sanskrit: nyāyopetā guṇopetāḥ sarvalokahitaiṣiṇaḥ santaḥ svargajitaḥ śuklāḥ saṃniviṣṭāś ca satpathe
english: Endowed with justice and virtue, desiring the good of all worlds, the pure good ones who have conquered heaven are established on the true path.

sanskrit: dātāraḥ saṃvibhaktāro dīnānugrahakāriṇaḥ sarvabhūtadayāvantas te śiṣṭāḥ śiṣṭasaṃmatāḥ
english: Those who give, who share equitably, who show grace to the wretched, who are compassionate toward all beings — they are the righteous, honored by the righteous.

sanskrit: sarvapūjyāḥ śrutadhanās tathaiva ca tapasvinaḥ dānanityāḥ sukhāṃl lokān āpnuvantīha ca śriyam
english: Those worthy of universal honor, rich in learning, and also the ascetics who are ever given to charity — they attain pleasant worlds and prosperity here as well.

sanskrit: pīḍayā ca kalatrasya bhṛtyānāṃ ca samāhitāḥ atiśaktyā prayacchanti santaḥ sadbhiḥ samāgatāḥ
english: Even at cost of hardship to their spouse and dependents, the good who gather with the good give beyond their means.

sanskrit: lokayātrāṃ ca paśyanto dharmam ātmahitāni ca evaṃ santo vartamānā edhante śāśvatīḥ samāḥ
english: Seeing the way of the world, dharma, and what is beneficial for the self, the good who live in this manner flourish for endless years.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā satyavacanam ānṛśaṃsyam athārjavam adroho nātimānaś ca hrīs titikṣā damaḥ śamaḥ
english: Non-violence, truthful speech, gentleness, uprightness, absence of malice, freedom from excessive pride, modesty, forbearance, self-restraint, and tranquility —

sanskrit: dhīmanto dhṛtimantaś ca bhūtānām anukampakāḥ akāmadveṣasaṃyuktās te santo lokasatkṛtāḥ
english: — those who are wise and steadfast, compassionate toward all beings, free from desire and hatred — they are the good ones, honored by the world.

sanskrit: trīṇy eva tu padāny āhuḥ satāṃ vṛttam anuttamam na druhyec caiva dadyāc ca satyaṃ caiva sadā vadet
english: They declare only three steps to be the unsurpassed conduct of the good: do no harm to anyone, always give, and always speak the truth.

sanskrit: sarvatra ca dayāvantaḥ santaḥ karuṇavedinaḥ gacchantīha susaṃtuṣṭā dharmyaṃ panthānam uttamam śiṣṭācārā mahātmāno yeṣāṃ dharmaḥ suniścitaḥ
english: The good who are compassionate everywhere, who know compassion, who go along here fully contented on the righteous, supreme path — great-souled ones of righteous conduct whose dharma is firmly established.

sanskrit: anasūyā kṣamā śāntiḥ saṃtoṣaḥ priyavāditā kāmakrodhaparityāgaḥ śiṣṭācāraniṣevaṇam
english: Freedom from envy, forbearance, peace, contentment, pleasant speech, and the abandonment of desire and anger — these are the practice of righteous conduct.

sanskrit: karmaṇā śrutasaṃpannaṃ satāṃ mārgam anuttamam śiṣṭācāraṃ niṣevante nityaṃ dharmeṣv atandritāḥ
english: Those endowed with learning through action, who tirelessly follow dharma, always practice the unsurpassed path of the good, which is righteous conduct.

sanskrit: prajñāprāsādam āruhya muhyato mahato janān prekṣanto lokavṛttāni vividhāni dvijottama atipuṇyāni pāpāni tāni dvijavarottama
english: Ascending the palace of wisdom and observing great masses of deluded people, and beholding the various activities of the world, O best of twice-born — the very sinful deeds among those are exceedingly meritorious, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yathāprajñaṃ yathāśrutam śiṣṭācāraguṇān brahman puraskṛtya dvijarṣabha
english: All this has been told to you, O brahmin, to the best of my wisdom and learning, placing foremost the virtues of righteous conduct, O bull among twice-born.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca sa tu vipram athovāca dharmavyādho yudhiṣṭhira yad ahaṃ hy ācare karma ghoram etad asaṃśayam
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then the Dharma-Hunter spoke to the brahmin, O Yudhiṣṭhira: 'That I indeed perform a terrible occupation — of this there is no doubt.'

sanskrit: vidhis tu balavān brahman dustaraṃ hi purākṛtam purākṛtasya pāpasya karmadoṣo bhavaty ayam doṣasyaitasya vai brahman vighāte yatnavān aham
english: 'But fate is powerful, O brahmin; what was done in a former life is hard to overcome; this fault of action arises from sin committed in a former life. And in overcoming this fault, O brahmin, I am indeed striving.'

sanskrit: vidhinā vihite pūrvaṃ nimittaṃ ghātako bhavet nimittabhūtā hi vayaṃ karmaṇo 'sya dvijottama
english: 'What has been ordained by fate in a former life — a killer may become the mere occasion for it; we are indeed only the occasion for this action, O best of twice-born.'

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ hatānāṃ māṃsāni vikrīṇāmo vayaṃ dvija teṣām api bhaved dharma upabhogena bhakṣaṇāt devatātithibhṛtyānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ pratipūjanāt
english: 'The flesh of those we slay and sell, O brahmin — dharma may arise even for them through its enjoyment and consumption, through the honoring of gods, guests, servants, and ancestors.'

sanskrit: oṣadhyo vīrudhaś cāpi paśavo mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ annādyabhūtā lokasya ity api śrūyate śrutiḥ
english: 'Herbs, plants, cattle, deer, and birds have become food and the like for the world — this too is heard in the Vedic teaching.'

sanskrit: ātmamāṃsapradānena śibir auśīnaro nṛpaḥ svargaṃ sudurlabhaṃ prāptaḥ kṣamāvān dvijasattama
english: 'By offering his own flesh, the forbearing king Śibi, son of Uśīnara, attained the very rare heaven, O best of twice-born.'

sanskrit: rājño mahānase pūrvaṃ rantidevasya vai dvija dve sahasre tu vadhyete paśūnām anvahaṃ tadā
english: 'In the royal kitchen of Rantideva in former times, O brahmin, two thousand animals were slaughtered daily.'

sanskrit: samāṃsaṃ dadato hy annaṃ rantidevasya nityaśaḥ atulā kīrtir abhavan nṛpasya dvijasattama cāturmāsyeṣu paśavo vadhyanta iti nityaśaḥ
english: 'Because Rantideva always gave food with meat, incomparable fame accrued to that king, O best of twice-born; at the four-monthly festivals animals were always slaughtered.'

sanskrit: agnayo māṃsakāmāś ca ity api śrūyate śrutiḥ yajñeṣu paśavo brahman vadhyante satataṃ dvijaiḥ saṃskṛtāḥ kila mantraiś ca te 'pi svargam avāpnuvan
english: '"The sacred fires too desire meat" — this also is heard in Vedic teaching. In sacrifices, O brahmin, animals are always slaughtered by twice-born; consecrated by mantras, those animals too are said to attain heaven.'

sanskrit: yadi naivāgnayo brahman māṃsakāmābhavan purā bhakṣyaṃ naiva bhaven māṃsaṃ kasya cid dvijasattama
english: 'If the sacred fires had never desired meat in former times, O brahmin, flesh would not have been food for anyone at all, O best of twice-born.'

sanskrit: atrāpi vidhir uktaś ca munibhir māṃsabhakṣaṇe devatānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca bhuṅkte dattvā tu yaḥ sadā yathāvidhi yathāśraddhaṃ na sa duṣyati bhakṣaṇāt
english: 'Even here the rule has been stated by sages regarding the eating of meat: one who always eats after offering to gods and ancestors, duly and with faith according to the rule, is not defiled by that eating.'

sanskrit: amāṃsāśī bhavaty evam ity api śrūyate śrutiḥ bhāryāṃ gacchan brahmacārī ṛtau bhavati brāhmaṇaḥ
english: '"One becomes a non-meat-eater in this way" — this also is heard in Vedic teaching; a brahmin who approaches his wife only in the fertile season is a celibate student.'

sanskrit: satyānṛte viniścitya atrāpi vidhir ucyate saudāsena purā rājñā mānuṣā bhakṣitā dvija śāpābhibhūtena bhṛśam atra kiṃ pratibhāti te
english: 'Having considered truth and untruth, a rule is stated here as well: in former times, human flesh was eaten by king Saudāsa who was overwhelmed by a curse. What do you think of that here, O brahmin?'

sanskrit: svadharma iti kṛtvā tu na tyajāmi dvijottama purākṛtam iti jñātvā jīvāmy etena karmaṇā
english: 'Considering this my own duty, I do not abandon it, O best of twice-born; knowing it as what was determined in a former life, I live by this occupation.'

sanskrit: svakarma tyajato brahmann adharma iha dṛśyate svakarmanirato yas tu sa dharma iti niścayaḥ
english: 'For one who abandons his own duty, adharma is seen here; but one who is devoted to his own duty — that is dharma, this is the certainty.'

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ hi vihitaṃ karma dehinaṃ na vimuñcati dhātrā vidhir ayaṃ dṛṣṭo bahudhā karmanirṇaye
english: 'The action ordained in a former life does not release the embodied being; this rule of the Creator has been seen in many ways in the determination of karma.'

sanskrit: draṣṭavyaṃ tu bhavet prājña krūre karmaṇi vartatā kathaṃ karma śubhaṃ kuryāṃ kathaṃ mucye parābhavāt karmaṇas tasya ghorasya bahudhā nirṇayo bhavet
english: 'A wise person engaged in cruel occupation must consider: how may I perform auspicious deeds? How may I be freed from defeat? The determination of that terrible karma may arise in many ways.'

sanskrit: dāne ca satyavākye ca guruśuśrūṣaṇe tathā dvijātipūjane cāhaṃ dharme ca nirataḥ sadā ativādātimānābhyāṃ nivṛtto 'smi dvijottama
english: 'In charity, in truthful speech, in service to my teacher, and in honoring the twice-born — I am always devoted to dharma; from excessive speech and excessive pride I have withdrawn, O best of twice-born.'

sanskrit: kṛṣiṃ sādhv iti manyante tatra hiṃsā parā smṛtā karṣanto lāṅgalaiḥ puṃso ghnanti bhūmiśayān bahūn jīvān anyāṃś ca bahuśas tatra kiṃ pratibhāti te
english: 'People think agriculture is good, yet great violence is considered inherent in it — those who plow with plows kill many creatures dwelling in the earth and many other living beings. What do you think of that here?'

sanskrit: dhānyabījāni yāny āhur vrīhy ādīni dvijottama sarvāṇy etāni jīvāni tatra kiṃ pratibhāti te
english: 'The grain seeds they speak of — rice and the rest, O best of twice-born — all these are living beings. What do you think of that here?'

sanskrit: adhyākramya paśūṃś cāpi ghnanti vai bhakṣayanti ca vṛkṣān athauṣadhīś caiva chindanti puruṣā dvija
english: 'Humans attack and kill cattle too and eat them; and they also cut down trees and plants, O brahmin.'

sanskrit: jīvā hi bahavo brahman vṛkṣeṣu ca phaleṣu ca udake bahavaś cāpi tatra kiṃ pratibhāti te
english: 'Many living beings are found in trees and fruits as well, and many also in water — what do you think of that here?'

sanskrit: sarvaṃ vyāptam idaṃ brahman prāṇibhiḥ prāṇijīvanaiḥ matsyā grasante matsyāṃś ca tatra kiṃ pratibhāti te
english: 'All this universe, O brahmin, is pervaded with living beings sustained by life; fish devour fish — what do you think of that here?'

sanskrit: sattvaiḥ sattvāni jīvanti bahudhā dvijasattama prāṇino 'nyonyabhakṣāś ca tatra kiṃ pratibhāti te
english: 'Beings live upon beings in many ways, O best of twice-born; living creatures eat one another — what do you think of that here?'

sanskrit: caṅkramyamāṇā jīvāṃś ca dharaṇīsaṃśritān bahūn padbhyāṃ ghnanti narā vipra tatra kiṃ pratibhāti te
english: 'While walking about, humans kill many living beings dwelling on the ground with their feet, O brahmin — what do you think of that here?'

sanskrit: upaviṣṭāḥ śayānāś ca ghnanti jīvān anekaśaḥ jñānavijñānavantaś ca tatra kiṃ pratibhāti te
english: 'Even sitting and lying down they kill living beings in many ways, and so do those possessed of knowledge and science — what do you think of that here?'

sanskrit: jīvair grastam idaṃ sarvam ākāśaṃ pṛthivī tathā avijñānāc ca hiṃsanti tatra kiṃ pratibhāti te
english: 'All this — sky and earth alike — is possessed by living beings; and out of ignorance they harm one another — what do you think of that here?'

sanskrit: ahiṃseti yad uktaṃ hi puruṣair vismitaiḥ purā ke na hiṃsanti jīvan vai loke 'smin dvijasattama bahu saṃcintya iha vai nāsti kaś cid ahiṃsakaḥ
english: 'What was declared as non-violence by astonished men in former times — who, while living in this world, does not do harm, O best of twice-born? Considering much, there is truly no one in this world who is non-violent.'

sanskrit: ahiṃsāyāṃ tu niratā yatayo dvijasattama kurvanty eva hi hiṃsāṃ te yatnād alpatarā bhavet
english: 'The ascetics devoted to non-violence, O best of twice-born, do commit harm; but through effort theirs becomes ever less.'

sanskrit: ālakṣyāś caiva puruṣāḥ kule jātā mahāguṇāḥ mahāghorāṇi karmāṇi kṛtvā lajjanti vai na ca
english: 'Invisible persons born in good families, endowed with great virtues, after performing very terrible deeds, truly feel no shame.'

sanskrit: suhṛdaḥ suhṛdo 'nyāṃś ca durhṛdaś cāpi durhṛdaḥ samyak pravṛttān puruṣān na samyag anupaśyataḥ
english: 'Friends do not see other friends rightly, nor do enemies see enemies rightly; they do not rightly observe those who behave properly.'

sanskrit: samṛddhaiś ca na nandanti bāndhavā bāndhavair api gurūṃś caiva vinindanti mūḍhāḥ paṇḍitamāninaḥ
english: 'Kinsmen do not rejoice with kinsmen in prosperity; and the foolish who fancy themselves learned even revile their teachers.'

sanskrit: bahu loke viparyastaṃ dṛśyate dvijasattama dharmayuktam adharmaṃ ca tatra kiṃ pratibhāti te
english: 'Much in the world is seen to be inverted, O best of twice-born — unrighteousness mingled with righteousness — what do you think of that here?'

sanskrit: vaktuṃ bahuvidhaṃ śakyaṃ dharmādharmeṣu karmasu svakarmanirato yo hi sa yaśaḥ prāpnuyān mahat
english: 'Much of various kinds can be said about deeds in the realm of dharma and adharma; but one who is devoted to his own duty shall attain great fame.'

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca dharmavyādhas tu nipuṇaṃ punar eva yudhiṣṭhira viprarṣabham uvācedaṃ sarvadharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: The Dharma-Hunter then spoke skillfully once more, O Yudhiṣṭhira — that best among all upholders of dharma spoke thus to the foremost of brahmins:

sanskrit: śrutipramāṇo dharmo hi vṛddhānām iti bhāṣitam sūkṣmā gatir hi dharmasya bahuśākhā hy anantikā
english: 'It has been said by elders that dharma has the Vedas as its authority; the course of dharma is subtle, with many branches and of unbounded scope.'

sanskrit: prāṇātyaye vivāhe ca vaktavyam anṛtaṃ bhavet anṛtaṃ ca bhavet satyaṃ satyaṃ caivānṛtaṃ bhavet
english: 'In a life-threatening situation and at a wedding, an untruth may be spoken; and an untruth may become truth, and truth itself may become untruth.'

sanskrit: yad bhūtahitam atyantaṃ tat satyam iti dhāraṇā viparyayakṛto 'dharmaḥ paśya dharmasya sūkṣmatām
english: 'What is supremely beneficial to beings — that is held to be truth; what produces the contrary is adharma. Observe the subtlety of dharma.'
